title: Employment outcome and predictors of competitive employment at 2-year follow-up of a vocational rehabilitation programme for individuals with schizophrenia in a high-income welfare society
source_filename: Employment outcome and predictors of competitive employment at 2-year follow-up of a vocational rehabilitation programme for individuals with schizoph.pdf
cohort_overlap_notes: Same 148 JUMP participants as gjerdalen2023 (5-year follow-up of the identical cohort); evensen2019 is the 69-participant register-consent subgroup; lystad2017 and klungsyr2021 analyse the 131 participants who completed neurocognitive assessment.
notes: Primary 2-year employment report for the JUMP cohort. Carries the only printed 2-year employment counts (31/37/20/58) and, in Figure 1, the only printed 2-year observation denominator (78 CBT + 61 CR = 139).

title: Exploring the potential cost-effectiveness of a vocational rehabilitation program for individuals with schizophrenia in a high-income welfare society
cohort_overlap_notes: The 69 JUMP participants (45 CBT + 24 CR) who consented to register extraction; a subgroup of the 148 in evensen2017 and gjerdalen2023.
notes: Status changed from linked_report to include: this report carries the ONLY cumulative-attainment result for the cohort (21/69 in paid employment at any point during the two-year follow-up), which no sibling report gives. Its Table 1 also supplies the independent confirmation of the 2-year observation denominator (chi-square df 3, n = 139). See manifest_changes.csv.

title: Vocational rehabilitation augmented with cognitive behavioral therapy or cognitive remediation for individuals with schizophrenia: a 5-year follow-up study
source_filename: Vocational rehabilitation augmented with cognitive behavioral therapy or cognitive remediation for individuals with schizophrenia  a 5-year follow-up .pdf
cohort_overlap_notes: Identical 148 JUMP participants as evensen2017, followed to 5 years by register linkage.
notes: Only 5-year report. Employment at 5 years is register-defined as having worked at least one month during the last calendar year, so it is PERIOD prevalence over a 12-month window and not comparable with the 2-year interview-based point prevalence. Also carries the four-timepoint occupational-outcome figure (Figure 1) whose post-intervention column is the cohort's only 9-18 month datapoint, and it is a percentage with no count.

title: G-estimation of causal pathways in vocational rehabilitation for adults with psychotic disorders - a secondary analysis of a randomized trial
cohort_overlap_notes: The 131 JUMP participants (68 CBT + 63 CR) with neurocognitive assessment; same analysis sample as lystad2017.
notes: report_quantifiable = no. The only occupational outcome is mean number of working hours per week (WHt) at baseline, 30 weeks and 100 weeks. No employment numerator or denominator of any kind is reported, so no outcome row is emitted. Retained as include per D10.2: eligible evidence the review cannot use, visible at the numerator/denominator gate. Useful for design provenance only: it states explicitly that each county was randomised to one of the two augmentations and that a non-augmented control group proved impossible to include.

title: Cognitive remediation and occupational outcome in schizophrenia spectrum disorders: A 2 year follow-up study
cohort_overlap_notes: The 131 JUMP participants with neurocognitive assessment; same analysis sample as klungsyr2021, subgroup of the 148 in evensen2017.
notes: report_quantifiable = no. Occupational status (working sheltered, work placement or competitively versus not working) at baseline, post treatment and follow-up appears ONLY in Figure 3, a 3-D bar chart with a percentage y-axis and no data labels; the text gives competitive employment as arm percentages (post treatment 10% CBT, 5% CR; follow-up 22% CBT, 16% CR) with no counts. Nothing is recoverable without back-calculation. Retained as the source of the construct definitions for competitive, sheltered and work-placement employment, which are quoted in the outcome rows.
